stories.title: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
stories.summary: Data centers are deeply unpopular. But what if we called them something else?

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
sources.text: Data centers are deeply unpopular . But what if we called them something else? Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too . The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “ the issue” in the presidential election. So OpenAI is to influence the AI debate moving forward, with Lehane discussing several proposals, including the development of AI “speed limits” ; finding ways to help people see AI as empowering them in their daily lives; pushing the U.S. to take a role in developing global standards; and yes — rebranding data centers as “AI compute campuses.” Lehane also described the conversation around data centers (a debate that has pushed Amazon and Microsoft to say they will no longer use NDAs in their negotiations with local governments ) as “good and healthy.” “Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects,” he said. sources.title: OpenAI wants to rebrand data centers as 'compute campuses' to try and win people over
sources.text: OpenAI is considering a new name for its biggest data centers as it looks to improve public perceptions of AI infrastructure amid ongoing political debate. Instead of calling them data centers, the ChatGPT maker is considering a rebrand to 'AI compute campuses' to give the facilities a name which sounds more economically positive. OpenAI hasn't directly announced these plans, however Axios reports that the changes could come as soon as this week, following US midterm elections on November 3 2026. It seems that the company is anticipating major political changes and the possibility that the Democrats regain control of the House of Representatives, which would result in a more challenging regulatory environment. OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane told Axios that he expects AI to be an ongoing political debate beyond the midterm elections. "Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects," he added. OpenAI has already been making efforts to win communities over, promising to partner with local communities to understand local needs. "We commit to paying our own way on energy, so that our operations don't increase your electricity prices," the company said at the start of 2026. A May 2026 report revealed that US states could face energy price hikes of between 6% and 29% by the end of the decades, and the US is already on course to re-open disused nuclear facilities to keep up with demand. But OpenAI's expansions are far from over. Stargate alone is a project anticipated to add 10GW of AI compute to the US by 2029, and it's still got just under halfway to go. stories.title: Elon Musk says Grok Bot was throttled as costs were ‘unsustainably high’
stories.summary: Grok Bot was throttled last week because Elon Musk said costs were ‘unsustainably high relative to revenue’

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Elon Musk says Grok Bot was throttled as costs were ‘unsustainably high’
sources.text: If you noticed that you burned through your Grok Bot usage much faster than usual in recent days, there’s a reason for that: Elon Musk intentionally limited users’ AI agent allowances in the face of “unsustainably high costs.” And as you’d expect, a lot of people are unhappy with that. The revelation came about after an X user pinged platform owner Musk , asking for a Grok Bot reset after they surprisingly hit their 100% usage limit, four days before it was due to reset. They additionally commented that “Normally I don’t even reach 100%.” Musk then replied to the post , stating: “The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue.” Many X users seemed irked by the situation, with several saying that their Grok Bot usage had hit the 100% limit while they were sleeping and not using any AI agents. Users claimed their usage had suddenly gone from 50% to 100%, 35% to 78%, and 70% to 100%, all supposedly without using Grok Bot at all. Elon Musk’s comments come amid broader scrutiny of the financial sustainability of many AI products. Tech stocks — including those of many leading AI firms — fell sharply last week as investors grew concerned over the profitability of the industry , with Google revealing that its own AI summaries have hurt its search advertising revenue. Concerns have also been raised in recent months over the finances involved in many AI companies’ offerings. For instance, users of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude Code can often spend many times more in tokens than they’re actually paying in monthly subscriptions, leading to questions over how sustainable many AI business models really are and whether things will need to be adjusted in the near future. This changing landscape hasn’t gone down well with many users, of course. One thread on Reddit dubbed Musk’s about-face an “indirect rug pull” of Grok Bot, with features and usage limited in a bid to cut costs. Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. But it’s unlikely that AI producers will be able to subsidize their products’ costs to users forever. Usage limits will necessarily need to tighten (as OpenAI quietly announced recently, much to the frustration of users ) and prices will need to increase for these business models to make sense. So don’t be surprised if Grok Bot’s lower cap is just the first of many big changes looming on the horizon. sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Elon Musk throttles Grok Bot limits due to ‘unsustainably high’ costs
sources.text: Over Halloween weekend, some Grok Bot users awoke to something especially spooky: Their weekly usage limits were unexpectedly maxed out, even if they hadn’t been using SpaceX’s agentic AI overnight. Some users reported on X that their usage jumped from as low as 50% to 100% . SpaceX CEO Elon Musk confirmed in an X post on Sunday that this was not a glitch. “The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue,” he wrote in a reply to a question from a user. He has not addressed the issue on his main feed but has continued boasting that Grok Bot can help you buy gifts for your family. Grok Bot has been positioned as a success story for the newly public SpaceX, which said in a filing last month that AI now makes up 52% of company income. Its renamed “Super Intelligence” division actually turned a profit of $431 million, which is a rarity in the AI industry. Its profit would’ve been higher if not for $1.2 billion of one-time costs related to its acquisition of Cursor . Musk recently referred to Grok Bot as having “the fastest growth of a product that I’ve ever seen in my life.” Musk has not yet shared how subscribers’ usage limits will be impacted moving forward. stories.title: OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs
stories.summary: OpenAI said that ChatGPT and Codex will draw usage from the same allocation pool after this change.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs
sources.text: The ChatGPT desktop app can be a confusing piece of software, given that there are ChatGPT and Codex sections, and within the former, there are Chat and Work tabs. With so many options, it’s sometimes easy to forget where you are working and where exactly your project is. In an apparent effort to address this, OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users. OpenAI said that initially, this experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely. “This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said. OpenAI also said with this transition, both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool. It said this change won’t impact most users, but based on usage and model, some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently. Rival Anthropic merged Claude’s chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September. sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: OpenAI combinará Chat y Work. Y hará realidad lo que muchos temían: ChatGPT y Codex compartirán los límites de uso
sources.text: Durante mucho tiempo, nuestra principal preocupación al abrir ChatGPT era conseguir una buena respuesta. Ahora hay otra pregunta que empieza a acompañar a quienes lo utilizan para algo más que conversar: cuánto margen queda antes de encontrarse con un límite . Y no porque todos los usuarios estén agotando sus cuotas, sino porque este tipo de herramientas han dejado de ser simples espacios para hacer preguntas y se han convertido en plataformas para analizar, crear y ejecutar trabajos completos. Hemos ganado posibilidades, sí, pero también hemos tenido que aprender un lenguaje de tokens y asignaciones que antes quedaba lejos de nuestras conversaciones. Ahora OpenAI ha anunciado un cambio concreto en la forma de utilizar sus herramientas. En un correo que hemos recibido, la compañía explica que empezará a probar en las próximas semanas una experiencia que reunirá Chat y Work, inicialmente con un grupo reducido y con vistas a ampliarla después. El anuncio incluye otra decisión: a partir de diciembre de 2026, ChatGPT y Codex compartirán una asignación de uso en los planes Plus, Pro y Business. Eso sí, la integración de las dos pestañas no supone la desaparición de Codex como experiencia independiente dentro de la aplicación de escritorio. Pongamos un ejemplo para entender las diferencias. Podemos abrir ChatGPT, subir un documento y pedirle que lo analice, pero también recurrir a Work para encargarle un trabajo más amplio que implique consultar archivos, utilizar aplicaciones y ejecutar diferentes pasos. Si lo que necesitamos es desarrollar software o modificar un proyecto de programación, entra en juego Codex, especializado precisamente en esas tareas. Son experiencias distintas, aunque no siempre estén tan separadas en lo que permiten hacer. Hasta ahora, esa distinción también se reflejaba en sus límites: Work y Codex compartían una asignación , mientras que los modelos del chat convencional tenían sus propios límites. Esa separación ofrecía cierto margen a los usuarios. En mitad de una tarea, ChatGPT podía sugerirnos continuar en Work , pero teníamos la posibilidad de aceptar la propuesta o permanecer en la conversación y utilizar los límites propios de Chat, sin recurrir a la asignación compartida de Work y Codex. No siempre obteníamos las mismas capacidades, aunque para determinados trabajos el resultado podía ser suficientemente parecido. Con el cambio anunciado, esa posibilidad de preservar la cuota de Work pierde parte de su utilidad: las operaciones realizadas con modelos incluidos en la nueva asignación también descontarán de ella, aunque decidamos seguir en Chat. La clave está en cómo se descontará ese consumo. Según OpenAI , no todas las peticiones tendrán el mismo peso: los modelos más avanzados y las operaciones complejas suelen consumir una mayor parte de la asignación disponible. La compañía habla de tokens, unidades de información que sus modelos procesan y generan, pero todavía no ha detallado cómo se traducirá el nuevo sistema en capacidad de uso para cada plan ni cuánto consumirán tareas concretas. Por tanto, no podemos establecer una equivalencia fiable en informes, conversaciones o proyectos. Cuando se agote la cuota, tocará esperar a que se restablezca o recurrir a las alternativas de pago disponibles. Hay una palabra que destaca especialmente en el comunicado: "ilimitado". La compañía asegura que el plan del destinatario incluye Instant sin consumir la nueva asignación, aunque su propia documentación establece restricciones frente al uso abusivo y mantiene límites específicos para determinadas funciones. Tampoco fija un umbral general y público que permita saber cuándo pueden aplicarse esas salvaguardas. Y hay otra cuestión importante: Instant puede resolver muchas necesidades cotidianas, pero no ofrece necesariamente las mismas capacidades que los modelos de razonamiento avanzado o las herramientas de trabajo autónomo. Para quienes utilizan ChatGPT como herramienta profesional, esa diferencia está lejos de ser un detalle menor. El correo contiene otra afirmación que merece especial atención. OpenAI prevé que la mayoría de los usuarios no tenga que esperar más a menudo para recuperar su asignación, aunque no explica cómo ha llegado a esa conclusión. Tampoco ofrece cifras que permitan comparar las condiciones actuales con las futuras. Es cierto que el 29 de octubre anunció una ampliación de las cuotas de Work y Codex para determinados planes Pro y Business Premium, pero no incluyó una mejora equivalente para Plus. Así que, de momento, tenemos una previsión tranquilizadora de la compañía y una pregunta sin respuesta: cuánto cambiará realmente la experiencia de quienes pagan por utilizar estas herramientas. Esta transformación no llega de la nada. Lo que comenzó en 2022 como un chatbot gratuito fue incorporando suscripciones como Plus , Team y Pro , hasta convertirse en una plataforma capaz de ejecutar trabajos que van mucho más allá de responder preguntas. También ha cambiado la escala económica del negocio: en mayo, Greg Brockman, presidente de OpenAI, declaró que la compañía esperaba gastar 50.000 millones de dólares en computación durante 2026, según Reuters . Es una cifra que ayuda a entender el coste de operar estos sistemas, aunque no demuestra que la nueva política de límites responda directamente a ese gasto. La prueba definitiva no llegará con el anuncio, sino cuando los suscriptores empiecen a trabajar bajo las nuevas condiciones. OpenAI señala que se podrá consultar la asignación disponible y su fecha de restablecimiento en Ajustes → Uso ; si se agota, las alternativas serán esperar, cambiar de plan o comprar créditos para las funciones compatibles. Son opciones concretas, pero no responden a la cuestión que queda abierta: cuánto trabajo avanzado permitirá realizar cada suscripción respecto a hoy. Hasta que conozcamos esas cifras y veamos su efecto, la integración será una promesa de comodidad con consecuencias todavía por medir. En Xataka | Google ha mejorado
